primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease (CKD stage 4/5) with chronic heart failure and ischemic heart disease

medications.purpose: Renoprotective RAAS blockade for CKD with proteinuria and hypertension control
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for all CKD/ESRD patients with proteinuria (ACR ≥30) and to monitor potassium and creatinine

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve target BP <130/80 mmHg in proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 advises BP control in CKD; CCBs are appropriate add‑on therapy

medications.purpose: Volume control in chronic congestive heart failure
medications.nice_justification: Guideline recommends managing fluid overload in CKD patients with CHF

medications.purpose: Hypertension management; synergistic natriuresis with ACE‑I
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 supports combined diuretic therapy for BP control in CKD

medications.purpose: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) management
medications.nice_justification: Guideline for CHF recommends beta‑blocker therapy; carvedilol preferred in HFrEF

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease
medications.nice_justification: Standard secondary‑prevention therapy; compatible with CKD

medications.purpose: Lipid lowering to reduce cardiovascular risk in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE recommends statin therapy for CKD patients (eGFR ≥30) and for IHD; continued despite low eGFR

medications.dose: 0.4 mg sublingual as needed for angina
medications.nice_justification: Guideline supports symptomatic angina management; no renal contraindication
Used for allergic symptoms; monitor anticholinergic load in elderly

medications.dose: 800 mg PO three times daily with meals
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 recommends phosphate binders for hyperphosphataemia in CKD/ESRD

medications.duration: Pending elevated PTH or vitamin D deficiency
medications.purpose: Treat secondary hyperparathyroidism or vitamin D deficiency
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 advises vitamin D analogues for secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD
NICE NG203 lists sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis in CKD

medications.duration: Pending Hb <100 g/L and symptomatic anaemia
medications.purpose: Treat CKD‑related anaemia after iron repletion
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 recommends ESA for CKD anaemia (Hb <100 g/L) after iron optimisation

medications.duration: Pending iron deficiency (Ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20%)
medications.purpose: Replete iron stores before ESA initiation
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 recommends IV iron for iron deficiency in CKD/ESRD

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive rise in serum creatinine and hyperkalaemia; dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy is contraindicated
Duplicate beta‑blockade increases risk of bradycardia, AV block, and hypotension
Combined loop and thiazide diuretics can cause volume depletion, hyponatraemia, and hypokalaemia
interactions_checked.action: Monitor electrolytes and volume status; consider reducing or stopping thiazide if signs of depletion

interactions_checked.interaction: Anticholinergic effects may be enhanced, causing dizziness or sedation in elderly
interactions_checked.action: Use diphenhydramine only as needed; consider alternative antihistamine with lower anticholinergic burden

contraindications.reason: Dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy is contraindicated (risk of hyperkalaemia and renal function decline) per NICE NG107/NG203
Duplicate beta‑blocker therapy with carvedilol; increases risk of bradycardia and hypotension
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue metoprolol; retain carvedilol for HFrEF

contraindications.reason: eGFR ~16 mL/min/1.73 m² is below NICE TA775 threshold (20–45) for SGLT2‑inhibitor use

assumptions_warnings: eGFR is low (15.9–18.7) but exact current value not provided; assumed ~16 mL/min/1.73 m² for dosing decisions

Serum potassium, phosphate, calcium, PTH, bicarbonate, haemoglobin and iron studies are not available – labs must be obtained before initiating phosphate binders, vitamin D analogue, sodium bicarbonate, ESA or IV iron
Blood pressure readings are missing – target <130/80 mmHg; BP must be measured to titrate antihypertensives
LVEF not documented – assumed HFrEF given carvedilol use; confirm before adding mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I or sulfonamide allergy before starting sevelamer or IV iron
Current use of over‑the‑counter NSAIDs not recorded – advise patient to avoid NSAIDs due to CKD
treatment_summary: Continue renoprotective ACE‑I (lisinopril) and antihypertensive regimen (amlodipine, furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide) while stopping losartan and metoprolol to avoid dual RAAS blockade and duplicate beta‑blockade. Maintain heart‑failure therapy (carvedilol), antiplatelet (clopidogrel), statin (simvastatin) and PRN nitroglycerin/diphenhydramine. Order missing labs (K+, PO4, Ca, PTH, HCO3‑, Hb, ferritin/TSAT, BP, weight, LVEF). If hyperphosphataemia, start sevelamer; if secondary hyperparathyroidism, start calcitriol; if metabolic acidosis, add sodium bicarbonate; if anaemia with iron deficiency, give IV iron followed by ESA. Avoid NSAIDs and SGLT2‑inhibitors due to low eGFR. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, BP and fluid status per NICE NG107/NG203 schedule.
